counterexamples.zeroSegmentation: segmentBits=0 reproduces the atomic search-body baseline and gives no segmentation benefit.
counterexamples.concentratedPartition: A deterministic concentrated-token fixture places all relevant tokens into one partition; segmentBits=6 then materializes the same search bytes as the monolithic search capability.

truthBoundary: v0.13 uses zero retention for segmented search because request-bound segment cache identity is not yet implemented.
The large reduction in declared runtime-body bytes does not equal the measured whole-process physical peak reduction.
At segmentBits=6 the measured ArrayBuffer peak is dominated by workspace-metadata-index after-materialize in all five memory samples.
The exact internal operation responsible for the metadata materialization peak has not yet been isolated, so no specific line-level cause is claimed.
Node external, heap and RSS are secondary process metrics and are not treated as direct equivalents of declared runtime-body bytes.
Hosted timing medians are observations for this fixture, not a universal speedup claim.
Segmentation provides no body reduction when relevant data is concentrated in a single partition.
strongestSupportedClaim: In this deterministic workspace harness, request-specific hash-prefix segmentation reduced the search runtime body from 837,720 B to 23,024 B at 64 partitions while preserving the exact seven-body report hash. The declared live runtime-body peak fell to 39,820 B, but measured ArrayBuffer peak fell only to 782,322 B because a different materialization phase, workspace-metadata-index, became the dominant measured peak.
